claims.text: Current experimental and computational baselines have limited accuracy for determining the target high-temperature properties of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Experimental reference data for relevant finite-temperature high-entropy-alloy behavior have limited availability.
Current experimental and computational approaches are inefficient across large high-entropy-alloy search spaces.
Machine-learning models, specifically deep-learning models, are the proposed intervention.
Deep learning will improve melting-temperature prediction relative to current experimental and computational baselines.
Deep learning will improve prediction of enthalpy of fusion relative to current baselines.
Deep learning will improve prediction of entropy of fusion relative to current baselines.
Deep learning will improve prediction of volume change upon melting relative to current baselines.
Deep learning will improve prediction of liquid thermodynamic properties relative to current baselines.
Deep learning will make determination of all listed properties more efficient across a large compositional space.
The proposed intervention applies to high-entropy alloys over a large compositional space.
The proposed scope includes high-temperature solid and liquid states.
Lattice distortions act as a structural mediator between use of deep learning and the predicted property improvements.
Configurational entropy acts as a structural mediator between use of deep learning and the predicted property improvements.
Machine-learning models can learn relationships between input features and target properties.
Learning feature-property relationships enables more accurate and efficient determination of the target properties.
Model performance may depend on the quality and quantity of training data.
Model performance may depend on architecture and hyperparameter choices.
